current_bottleneck: Final-path joint-distribution finetuning is clean and literature-aligned, but it does not improve the broad-frame risk scenario law. It ties same-frame 510a at 5/11 while worsening coverage, conditionality, level KS, median bias, bad-window rate, persistent undercoverage, and kurtosis. The objective improves a few geometry metrics but narrows usable conditional uncertainty.
last_result_summary: 596a kept the 510a AR flow architecture unchanged and finetuned from the 510a final checkpoint with full-path energy plus sliced projection Wasserstein and a small FM anchor. Focused tests passed. Training selected epoch 3. Broad-frame full-suite score was 5/11, failing coverage, conditionality, time_series, regime_coverage, distributional_fidelity, and mean_reversion. Relative to same-frame 510a: coverage90 worsened 69.6% to 65.7%, h30 66.2% to 61.2%, conditional MAE reduction 7.61% to 5.58%, worst-cell MAE -13.1% to -18.1%, kurtosis ratio 0.618 to 0.584, persistent undercoverage 16.2% to 18.8%, level KS 3/25 to 2/25, median-bias cells 10/25 to 6/25, bad-window rate 24.0% to 29.7%. Mean-reversion active corr improved 0.531 to 0.581 and pathwise max-jump KS improved 0.463 to 0.456, but not enough.
next_step_recommendation: Do not weight-sweep 596a by default. The next principled step is to diagnose whether the missing uncertainty is sampling/noise calibration in the existing AR flow or a learned transition-law limitation. Prefer a small inference/training noise calibration diagnostic over another architecture change.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 510a and 596a both score 5/11, but 510a is the better risk profile because 596a narrows coverage and worsens distributional fidelity. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product.
